title: Review: First law of thermodynamics and p–V work; Thermodynamic processes and heat engines; Specific heat capacity and latent heat; Entropy and the second law; Electric charge and charging; Coulomb's law
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Physics 2 (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: F01-1#t4 term and clue written for the game; F02-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; F02-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; F01-1#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: F01-1#N.12a, F02-1#N.13, T09-1#N.13, F02-1#N.12a, F01-1#N.10, F02-1#N.4, T02-1#N.10, T07-1#N.3c, T08-1#N.3b, T09-1#N.2b, F01-1#N.7, F02-1#N.10. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Neutron
items.clue: Particle that carries no charge at all.

items.label: Resultant
items.clue: Single force found by adding each separate force as vectors.

items.label: Repulsion
items.clue: What happens between like charges, such as two positive ones.

items.label: Electron
items.clue: Negative particle that an object gains or loses to become charged.

questions.stem: A rod on an insulating handle has a charge of −6.0 nC. It touches a neutral metal sphere on an insulating stand and is then pulled away. Nothing else touches either object. Afterwards, the rod's charge is −2.0 nC. What is the charge on the sphere?

For two small charged spheres a distance r apart, the magnitude of the electric force between them divided by the magnitude of the gravitational force between them is R. The charge on each sphere is then halved, the mass of each sphere is doubled, and the separation is increased to 3r. What is the new value of this ratio?

options.text: R

questions.stem: A gas in a cylinder is in good thermal contact with a large water bath. The gas is compressed very slowly, so its temperature stays constant. Which statement about the entropy changes is correct?

options.text: The entropies of the gas and of the bath stay the same, because the temperature does not change.
The entropy of the gas increases, because work is done on it during the compression.
The gas's entropy decreases and the bath's increases, so the total does not decrease.
The gas's entropy decreases and the bath's is unchanged, so the total entropy decreases.

questions.stem: Two small charged spheres, 1 and 2, exert electric forces of magnitude F on each other. The charge on sphere 2 is doubled, and the distance between the spheres is tripled. What is the magnitude of the force now exerted on sphere 2 by sphere 1?

A negatively charged rod is held near a neutral metal sphere on an insulating stand, and the sphere is connected to ground by a wire. This time the rod is taken away first, and only then is the wire removed. What is the final charge on the sphere?

options.text: Positive, as electrons flowed away through the wire while the rod was near.
Zero, as electrons flow back through the wire once the rod is gone.
Negative, as charge from the rod passes to the sphere through the air.
Negative, as the wire leaves the sphere with the same sign as the rod.

questions.explanation: The order matters. The wire must be removed while the rod is still near, to trap the charge; here the sphere ends neutral.

questions.stem: Two small charged spheres whose centres are 0.60 m apart exert electric forces of magnitude 1.0 N on each other. Their charges do not change. At what centre-to-centre separation would the forces have a magnitude of 9.0 N?

0.20 kg of water and 0.20 kg of cooking oil, both at 20 °C, are each supplied with 12 kJ of energy. Specific heat capacities: water 4180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, oil 2000 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹. Assume no energy is lost. Which statement about their final temperatures is correct?

options.text: The oil ends at 50 °C and the water at about 34 °C.
The water ends at 50 °C and the oil at about 34 °C.
They end at the same temperature, as each gets 12 kJ.
The oil ends at 30 °C and the water at about 14 °C.

questions.stem: A gas in a cylinder is compressed by a piston. During the compression, 250 J of work is done on the gas, and 400 J of energy is transferred from the gas to its surroundings by cooling. What is the change in the internal energy of the gas?

An ideal gas in a cylinder is compressed slowly, so that its temperature stays constant. The work done on the gas during the compression is W, which is positive. Which statement about the energy transferred by heating or cooling is correct?

options.text: Energy equal to W is transferred into the gas by heating.
No energy is transferred, since the temperature stays fixed.
Less than W leaves by cooling; the rest is stored in the gas.
Energy equal to W is transferred out of the gas by cooling.

questions.stem: A moving car brakes to a stop. Treat the car, its brakes, the road and the air as an isolated system. Which statement correctly compares the system after the car stops with the system before?

options.text: The total energy is less, because some was used up in stopping the car.
The total energy is the same, but less of it is available to do work.
The total energy is the same, and all of it is still available to do work.
The total entropy is the same, because the total energy is the same.

questions.stem: Predict first. A polythene rod is rubbed with a dry wool cloth and gains a charge of −8.0 nC. Which statement about the cloth after the rubbing is correct?

options.text: Its charge is −8.0 nC, because rubbing charges both surfaces in the same way.
Its charge is +8.0 nC, as the electrons the rod gained came from the cloth.
It is uncharged, because the friction created the charge on the rod alone.
Its charge is +8.0 nC, because protons moved from the rod to the cloth.

questions.stem: Two protons are a distance r apart. What is the ratio F_E/F_g of the magnitude of the electric force between them to the magnitude of the gravitational force between them? Use k = 9.0 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻², ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² C² N⁻¹ m⁻², G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻², e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, m_p = 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg, and m_e = 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg.
